html:
The Göktürks, or Türks, were a Turkic people of Inner Asia who built the first great Turkic empire, the Turkic Khaganate, from 552 to 744. The map shows their eastern realm on the Mongolian steppe in 600 and 700.

They had been ironworkers for the Rouran in the Altai. In 552 their leader Bumin overthrew the Rouran, and within a few years the Türks ruled from Manchuria to the Black Sea. Their empire soon split into an eastern half on the Mongolian steppe and the Western Turkic Khaganate in Central Asia. Both grew rich from Silk Road trade and tribute from China.

The Tang dynasty conquered the eastern Türks in 630, but they rose again in 682 and founded the Second Turkic Khaganate. Its rulers raised the Orkhon inscriptions, the oldest known texts in a Turkic language, praising princes such as Kul Tigin. In 744 the Uyghurs destroyed them. The name Turk spread from them to many peoples. See also the chart's Türk Khaganates.
